label: Readout-phase unit favoring inputs s/<DEL>/j/r/v/l/3
explanation: Almost only active in the readout: the delimiter step and copy phase hold 94% of the activation mass (original phase 6%, never at t=0). Within the readout it depends on which token is being input. The input s is the strongest trigger (31% firing rate, 26% of mass, and the top examples are s fed back right after <DEL>). <DEL> comes next (15%), then j, r, 3, v, l. It also fires more on early recall positions (recall_idx 0-3, about 77% of mass) and on outputs u/f/0/b/d. The predicate (readout and input in {s,j,r,v,l,3,<DEL>}) covers about 70% of mass but its precision is only about 21%. The unit fires on only a minority of steps that match, so the token and position effects look graded and spread out, not like a crisp rule. It is essentially silent in the original phase after the first few steps, and silent on most copy steps whose input is a vowel or a common letter. Combining input-token sets with early position or output-token sets did not push F1 above 0.33.
